facts.raw_span: skin fragility since early infancy
Symptoms improved in winter and worsened in summer
Mild xerosis with superficial skin erosions
Erythematous residual macules from previous erosions
Some lesions had unusual linear geographic contour
Lesions predominantly located at areas of friction
No history of blistering
Serological markers for celiac disease were negative
Complete separation of the stratum corneum
Clean split just above the stratum granulosum
2 heterozygous mutations in exon 2 of the CDSN gene
Normal results for: Collagen IV and VII, α6 and β4 integrines, Laminine-332

concepts.why: The patient's skin fragility since early infancy, complete separation of the stratum corneum, and clean split just above the stratum granulosum are consistent with peeling skin syndrome, which is also supported by the 2 heterozygous mutations in exon 2 of the CDSN gene.

The patient's symptoms improving in winter and worsening in summer, mild xerosis with superficial skin erosions, and lesions predominantly located at areas of friction are consistent with keratolysis exfoliativa.

The patient's skin fragility since early infancy, unusual linear geographic contour of some lesions, and 2 heterozygous mutations in exon 2 of the CDSN gene are consistent with acral peeling skin syndrome.
The patient's symptoms improving in winter and worsening in summer, and lesions predominantly located at areas of friction are consistent with focal acral hyperkeratosis.
The patient's mild xerosis with superficial skin erosions, and lesions predominantly located at areas of friction are consistent with exfoliative keratolysis.
The patient's skin fragility since early infancy, complete separation of the stratum corneum, and 2 heterozygous mutations in exon 2 of the CDSN gene are consistent with peeling skin disease.

The negative serological markers for celiac disease and normal immunofluorescence mapping results for collagen IV and VII, α6 and β4 integrines, and laminine-332, along with the clinical presentation of skin fragility and peeling, are consistent with peeling skin syndrome type B.

rationales.F01: Skin fragility since early infancy suggests a genetic condition, which is consistent with peeling skin syndrome.
rationales.F02: Seasonal variation in symptoms could indicate a condition that worsens with heat or humidity, such as acral peeling skin syndrome.
rationales.F05: Unusual linear geographic contour of lesions is a distinctive feature of peeling skin syndrome.
rationales.F06: Lesions located at areas of friction suggest a condition that is exacerbated by mechanical stress, such as acral peeling skin syndrome.
rationales.F09: Complete separation of the stratum corneum is a characteristic histopathological feature of peeling skin syndrome.
rationales.F10: Clean split just above the stratum granulosum is a characteristic histopathological feature of peeling skin syndrome.
rationales.F11: Heterozygous mutations in the CDSN gene are associated with peeling skin syndrome.
